pull.title: descriptor: Expose key expression parsing
pull.body:
This PR exposes a utility function to parse and validate a standalone descriptor key expression. 
This is particularly useful in GUI multisig setup flows where the UI accepts a pasted key expression. The GUI can use this parser to validate input, inspect the parsed key,  and apply setup-specific policy i.e. reject private keys, uncompressed keys etc. (Multisig Wizard tracking issue: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/35645)

`PubkeyProvider` is the existing internal representation of a parsed key expression. This PR exposes its interface in `descriptor.h` and adds a public `ParsePubkey()` overload that returns the providers produced by the existing parser.

Key changes
- public overload uses P2TR key rules, permitting compressed, x-only, extended, and MuSig key expressions while rejecting uncompressed keys.
- Add `GetOriginInfo()` for retrieving explicitly provided key origin information.

---
Also, while I'm here, I noticed that `musig` parser accepted trailing characters apart from `/`. 
- Add a fix & test to reject unexpected trailing characters after a `musig()` expression

events.message:
descriptor: Reject trailing text after musig()

The musig() parser split the input at the closing parenthesis without
validating the remaining text. This allowed unexpected characters after
the expression to be ignored.
Add a requirement for nonempty char after musig() to begin with '/'.

descriptor: move PubkeyProvider to descriptor.h

Expose the abstract interface by moving to descriptor.h to allow other
modules to consume parsed key expressions.
Mostly a move-only commit. Implementation of operator< is retained in
descriptor.cpp

descriptor: Add public ParsePubKey overload

Add an overload for parsing standalone key expressions using P2TR key
rules.
Also, expose explicitly provided origin information through GetOriginInfo(),
allowing callers to inspect the fingerprint and derivation path without
re-parsing the expression.

events.body: Rebased  & force-pushed to https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35918/commits/17ddfdc0edc3ac35b1a87c884d61db2a58941bce. No other changes.

The first commit, 7835e0ef70, fixes a bug I also found on v31.1: `tr(musig(X)xyz)` is accepted and `xyz` is dropped. The worse case is a typo such as `tr(musig(X)0/*)`, missing the `/`, which v31.1 turns into a non-ranged `tr(musig(X))` without an error. Since it is a parser fix and the rest of the PR adds a new API, would you split it into its own PR? It could then be reviewed and backported on its own.

Concept ACK

A couple of nits in commits:

- In 2nd commit (c17a6ab) message body, it mentions "Mostly a move-only commit. Implementation of operator< is retained in descriptor.cpp" but there's no operator< in `descriptor.cpp` or `descriptor.h`. What remains in the .cpp are the implementations of `HavePrivateKeys()` and `DetermineApostropheUse()`. Perhaps a leftover of a previous version of this change?

- In 3rd commit (17ddfdc), tiny nit: the title specifies ParsePubKey but the function name is `ParsePubkey`.

Please keep in mind that #36442 changes the internal `ParsePubkey` to return a single provider for multipath expressions, so the new public overload may need to follow, depending on which one gets merged first.

I left another couple of non-blocking nits inline.

comments.body: Using P2TR here is intentional, as mentioned in the PR description. Its key parsing rules match what we want for standalone key expressions: accept compressed, x-only, extended, and musig() expressions, while rejecting uncompressed keys.

nit: "P2TR key rules" may not be obvious to callers, so perhaps spell out what it means, and that multipath returns more than one provider (?):
```suggestion
/** Parse a key expression using P2TR key rules: compressed, x-only, extended and
* musig() key expressions are accepted, uncompressed keys are rejected, and
* WIF private keys are serialized as x-only.
```

nit: maybe worth noting that it only covers the key's own origin, e.g. a musig() returns none even when its participants have one (there's no test for this yet; I'll suggest one later with some other test cases): 
```suggestion
    /** Return explicitly provided key origin information, if any. For musig(), this
     *  does not include its participants' origins. */
```
